title: Citrine Labs — tokenflow and SLA pathfinding
summary: Discovery to map Citrine's p95 latency and concurrency targets for a streaming chat product; evaluated hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs, token/sec benchmarking approach, and security/compliance needs. Agreed to run a 2-week pilot benchmark with Redwood-hosted config and a follow-up deep-dive for dedicated sizing.
topics: p95 latency targets (first-token vs streaming steady-state)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46m
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Connor Liu (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO, Citrine), Devon Park (Lead ML Eng), Samir Khan (SRE), Priya Mehta (Product)

Summary (auto): map latency objectives, confirm workloads, agree pilot steps, surface security blockers.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, i'm Maya from Redwood, this is Connor our solutions engineer. how are you all?
[00:12] Lena: good, yep thanks, we've been trying to line up the tokenflow numbers before our Q4 release.
[00:20] Devon: apologies for the late join, had a build, but we're all here.
[00:28] Maya: quick agenda - get your p95 targets, traffic shape, hosting preferences and any security must-haves. then Connor will run through how we benchmark and what artifacts we need.
[00:40] Samir: sounds good, i want to be clear on the p95 we care about, is that first-token latency or whole-stream? we stream incremental tokens.
[00:50] Connor: good call. we usually separate first-byte/first-token cold-start and steady-state per-token latency. for streaming chat customers often target first-token p95 under 300ms and per-token steady-state under 80-120ms depending on sequence length and model.
[01:10] Devon: for us the SLAs are tighter — product wants p95 first-token <220ms and streaming token cadence such that a user sees a token every 70-100ms on average. our model is a 13B instruction-tuned one with 1k context windows.
[01:30] Priya: product will measure perceived latency as time to first meaningful token and then token cadence. if the cadence is slow it's a bad UX even if total completion time is ok.
[01:44] Maya: noted. what about concurrency? how many simultaneous streams at peak?
[01:48] Lena: peak concurrency around 1.2k active users, but multiplexing on the frontend means about 1.8k open streams at peak. most are short, 8–12 tokens per response on average, some long tails.
[02:05] Samir: plus burst spikes during campaign launches — saw 3x baseline for 4–6 minutes last month.
[02:12] Connor: ok that shapes both batching and routing logic. Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private: any initial leaning?
[02:20] Devon: we'd prefer hosted to iterate quickly but the security team requires SOC 2 type II and customer data residency controls; dedicated or private might be needed for certain customers.
[02:32] Maya: Redwood hosted meets SOC2 — we can send the attestation. for private/dedicated we support VPC peering and bring-your-own-KMS, HSM integrations. sometimes teams start on hosted for speed then transition to dedicated for predictability.
[02:48] Lena: two quick items: can we get token/sec numbers per GPu for our 13B tuned model? and what's the quantization impact?
[02:58] Connor: rough ballpark - unquantized single A100-like instance might do 250–450 tokens/sec for a 13B in a streaming steady-state depending on attention emulation and sequence length. with int8 quant and kernel opt you can push up 1.6x-2x, but that trades off a small quality delta. prefix/KV cache helps if many sessions repeat prompts.
[03:25] Devon: that's close to what we estimated. our open infra uses batching at the edge, but we worry about latency when batching too aggressively. how does Redwood balance batching vs latency?
[03:34] Connor: we have continuous batching plus latency SLO windows; you can set a max batching delay (e.g., 10ms) and a latency SLO that triggers bypass to lower-latency routing or smaller batch sizes. also automatic prefix cache bypass so repeated prompts are served quickly.
[03:52] Samir: what about model variant routing and graceful degradation if capacity is saturated during spikes? we can't have 503s.
[03:59] Maya: Redwood supports routing by policy. typical pattern: route to hosted fastest model; if capacity constrained, failover to lower-cost quantized variant or lower-sized model. for critical tenants we recommend dedicated pools with reserved capacity. we also support regional fallback to maintain availability.
[04:18] Priya: do you have hard numbers on p95 at 1.2k concurrent streams for streaming?
[04:25] Connor: it depends on GPU mix and whether you use multiplexing. approximate baseline: with dedicated GPU pool sized for 1.2k streams (majority short responses) and Q8 quant, you can reach p95 first-token ~200–300ms; worst-case long-context completions push that higher. for hosted you can run a pilot to measure exact metrics — that's what we propose.
[04:47] Devon: pilot, yes — what data do you need?
[04:51] Maya: we usually ask for a traffic simulator config (histogram of session lengths, tokens per response, arrival rate), and sample prompt set. we'll run token/sec synthetic workload against our hosted infra with your model or a close match.
[05:04] Lena: we can't share the model weights. can you run against a Redwood-verified 13B proxy model with similar perf characteristics?
[05:12] Connor: absolutely, we have verified closest-match models in the catalog. results are directional but give a predictable sizing baseline. if you later want a dedicated pilot we can mount your model in a Private environment under NDA.
[05:25] Samir: security question — SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, and KMS. we need to ensure logs are retained for 90 days and KMS keys are customer-managed. how is that handled in hosted?
[05:37] Maya: hosted supports SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC. audit logs are available; retention beyond default is an add-on. KMS customer-managed keys are supported for Private and Dedicated; hosted can integrate with BYOK for certain customers — we can share the security pack.
[05:50] Devin: (sic) can you share SOC2 and penetration test findings?
[05:54] Maya: yes — we'll attach SOC 2 attestation and redacted pentest summary.
[06:00] Priya: ok for pilot timeline, we want results in 10 business days. is that realistic?
[06:05] Connor: yes, a 7–10 day hosted benchmark run is typical if we have the simulator and prompts.
[06:12] Lily: (background)
[06:16] Devon: for concurrency shaping — our front end holds websockets open. would you recommend muxing multiple users to a single token stream or 1:1 streams?
[06:25] Connor: recommended: keep 1:1 logical streams for UX, but multiplexing at the transport level can reduce overhead. Redwood's runtime maintains per-session KV cache so multiplexing doesn't hurt cache locality as long as contexts are pinned appropriately.
[06:40] Samir: what about cold-starts after scaling events? we saw 600ms p95 spikes when we ramped capacity in last release. can Redwood do warm pools?
[06:50] Maya: yes, dedicated supports warm standby pools and cold-start mitigation; hosted has warm nodes but you can also configure minimum replica counts in Dedicated to reduce cold starts. autoscaling policies can be tuned to keep latency SLOs during ramp.
[07:05] Devon: how do you measure p95 for streaming which is continuous? do you take first-token p95 and a separate per-token p95 over stream?
[07:14] Connor: exactly. first-token p95 and inter-token p95 in steady-state. we also report token-per-second throughput and percentile of time-between-tokens. dashboards can break down by model, route, and token-range.
[07:30] Priya: you mentioned quantization quality trade-offs. have customers done AB tests for generation quality vs quant gain?
[07:36] Connor: yes, we often run A/B with prompt evals and ngram overlap metrics; for many instruction-tuned 13Bs int8 has minimal quality impact on typical prompt sets, but always verify with your test prompts. Redwood Optimize can recommend quant configs per workload.
[07:54] Lena: what about cost modeling — we need cost per million tokens estimates for hosted vs dedicated with reserved capacity.
[08:02] Maya: we'll share a cost model spreadsheet. hosted gives easy start but per-token can be higher at scale; dedicated with reserved capacity reduces unit cost but requires commit. we'll share modeled scenarios for your 1.2k concurrency baseline.
[08:17] Devon: demo question — can you stream tokens back over our websocket? do you support SSE/websocket streaming plus function/tool calling?
[08:25] Connor: yes streaming via chunked responses over HTTP and websocket SSE for real-time UIs. function-calling is supported; we can show examples in the follow-up demo.
[08:34] Samir: curious about caching strategy — if many similar prompts, how much saving can we expect?
[08:39] Connor: prefix/KV caching can reduce compute on repeated prefixes by up to 40-60% depending on prompt overlap. caching is most effective for system messages and consistent instruction templates.
[08:52] Priya: ok for next steps — make sure we capture exact traffic histogram.
[08:56] Maya: agreed. we'll enumerate artifacts needed. we'll also propose pilot config and dedicated sizing if pilot shows sustained high utilization.
[09:04] Lena: also include SLA language for p95s and fallback behaviors.
[09:08] Maya: noted — will include proposed SLA windows and fallback policy templates.
[09:12] Devon: any constraints on tokenization differences? we use a custom tokenizer; does that change token/sec numbers?
[09:18] Connor: tokenization affects tokens/sec obviously; we'll ask for average token length in characters and run with your sample prompts (or simulate with a proxy) so numbers map to your tokenizer.
[09:29] Samir: will you provide a public benchmark report after pilot?
[09:33] Maya: yes we provide a pilot report with p50/p90/p95 latencies, token/sec, cost per million tokens, and recommendations.
[09:41] Priya: perfect.
[09:44] Lena: one more security nuance — some customers require e-discovery logs and data residency in EU. for hosted, is there a regional isolation option?
[09:53] Maya: yes, hosted in EU region is available; for strict data residency and isolated control plane we'd recommend Private. we'll document the differences.
[10:02] Devon: ok i'm going to outline a tentative pilot: 7–10 days on Redwood hosted using a 13B proxy, traffic shaped to our histogram with a 3x spike window, collect p95 for first-token and inter-token, plus cost calc.
[10:17] Connor: that works. we'll also attach a steering doc for configs like max batch delay, multiplexing settings, quantization toggles.
[10:28] Maya: are we good to commit to the pilot and a follow-up dedicated sizing review?
[10:33] Lena: yes, pending the NDA and security docs.
[10:37] Samir: timeline wise, share the pilot plan today, we'll kick off Monday.
[10:41] Maya: perfect. we'll share benchmark spreadsheet, SOC2, and a pilot config by EOD.
[10:48] Priya: thanks all.
[10:50] Maya: recap — we'll run pilot, deliver report, then dedicated sizing if needed. thanks everyone.

Notes: occasional transcription errors present; names occasionally mis-annotated by auto transcribe. References shared: https://redwood.app/share/benchmarks/citrine-2027 and security pack https://redwood.app/sec/citrine-security-pack.pdf
